item.title: Gov Mbah: How Tinubu’s reforms halted Nigeria’s economic collapse
item.description: …Says shared prosperity follows Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, says Nigeria would have suffered total economic collapse but for President Bola Tinubu’s courageous reforms, arguing that the removal of fuel subsidy and floating of the naira only waited until the President’s assumption of office in 2023 because the nation delayed the ‘evil day’ and lived on borrowed time. He gave the insights at the weekend during the launch of “As Tinubu Mbah Moves” (ATM), a support group convened by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN), and dedicated to the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Mbah in Enugu. Speaking to the mammoth crowd, he said, “It would have been a lot easier for any leader to just continue with the status quo and carry on on the basis of business as usual. But for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it was business unusual that led to the bold initiatives. “As a person who had played very actively in the oil and gas sector, I had written quite a lot of features and articles arguing against the fuel subsidy regime long before now, for it was clear to me, even from the point of a major player in that sector, that the subsidy regime was not sustainable because of the economic devastation it was causing to us as Nigerians. We were just basically postponing the evil day. “We were just digging our poverty pits continually. We were actually digging deeper into that pit of poverty. And it would have taken a very courageous leader in his first term to say, ‘Look, if we have to build for the future, if we have to think about our children, then we must take out the subsidy and we must also unify the exchange rate regime.’” Mbah took a swipe at the foreign exchange regime before the floating of the naira by Tinubu, describing it as a cesspool of corruption. “We got to a point in this country where even salary earners, once they get paid, would run to the bureau de change to change it rather than hold their salary in naira. Confidence was completely eroded in the naira. Nobody wanted to touch it with the tip of their finger. And that was the recipe for a failed nation. “If you wanted to do a study or research of any failed nation, it is when the country, the citizens themselves, begin to lose confidence in their currency. And that was the environment that this President inherited. “It was a major cesspool of corruption. The arbitrage was obvious and people were being taken advantage of. What was happening between the official and the parallel market was terrible. And some people were benefiting from that arbitrage at the expense of the economy. But it took this President’s understanding of the economy to be able to make those bold decisions,” he explained. item.title: Photos: Ronaldinho returns to professional football at age 46
item.description: Greying and rounder in the face than during his prime, Ronaldinho made a winning return to professional football on Sunday for Ravenna, an ambitious club in Italy’s third tier aiming to reach Serie A. Under the watchful eye of Ignazio Cipriani, the Italian-American businessman who has owned the club since 2024, Ronaldinho perfectly played his role as the centrepiece of a clever PR stunt. Brazilian football star Ronaldinho waves to supporters at half-time during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano RELLANDINI / AFP) The 46-year-old Brazilian great put in a low-key performance in his first competitive match since playing for Fluminense in 2015, as Ravenna, bidding for promotion to Serie B, beat local rivals Forli 2-0 in front of a packed Stadio Bruno Benelli on Italy’s Adriatic coast. Ravenna’s Giulio Donati (L) celebrates after scoring with Brazilian football star Ronaldinho (top) during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano RELLANDINI / AFP) Known for his dynamic dribbling and often outrageous ball control in his heyday, Ronaldinho largely strolled around the pitch and laid off simple passes to his teammates, who would once upon a time not have been anywhere near his level as players. Ronaldinho’s arrival has given Ravenna a previously unimaginable profile, and Cipriani would no doubt have been delighted to see the pack of reporters and photographers that descended on the Benelli. Brazilian football star Ronaldinho looks on during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano RELLANDINI / AFP) The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner only played in the first half but was involved in the move which ended with Giulio Donati smashing hosts Ravenna ahead in the 36th minute. Ronaldinho entered the field to great fanfare, with the 5,000-capacity Benelli having a temporary stand with 1,800 places — dubbed “R10” — added for the occasion. Brazilian football star Ronaldinho answers journalists at half-time during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano Rellandini / AFP) Flares and smoke bombs were let off in the stands while Andrea Bocelli’s “Con Te Partiro” blasting out of the stadium’s speakers. And he left after the first half, but not before plenty of handshakes with his teammates and match officials. Only he knows whether he will play for Ravenna again, although he had only taken part in a single training session with his teammates before this one-off appearance. He only arrived in Italy a few days before Sunday’s match, suggesting that he hasn’t committed himself for the long haul. item.title: My relationship with Kogi Central goes beyond elections – Natasha
item.description: John Alechenu Senator Natasha Hadiza Akpoti-Uduaghanb has kickstarted her 2027 re-election campaign with a clear call to her constituents: vote, and be prepared to protect your votes. Speaking with confidence about her re-election bid, the federal lawmaker said her relationship with the people of Kogi Central Senatorial District went beyond elections. Her Media Aide, Sam Idoko, in a statement on Sunday, quoted her as telling thousands of supporters at a campaign event in Ihima: “My relationship with the people of Kogi Central goes beyond elections. These are my people, my family and the very reason I remain committed to public service. I do not need an election season to remember where I come from.” The campaign commenced in October with roadside receptions across Okene and adjoining areas before culminating in a major gathering at her residence in Obeiba, Ihima, Okehi Local Government Area. The motorcade passed through Itakpe, Kabba Junction, Ogaminana, the PDP Secretariat, Agassa Roundabout and Obehira. At every stop, residents and party faithful lined the route to welcome her. In Ihima, thousands gathered and many stayed late into the night. More than 500 supporters travelled from Abuja to be there. Her husband, High Chief Emmanuel Uduaghan, was beside her. Alhaji MJ Akpata Aliu was present. PDP candidates for the House of Representatives in Adavi/Okehi, Ajaokuta and Okene/Ogori-Magongo, and candidates for the State Assembly, also attended. Natasha said, “What we witnessed today is a reflection of the bond we have continued to build over time. I am deeply grateful to everyone who came out, not because they were compelled to do so, but because they believe in the journey we have undertaken together.” In Ajaokuta and Geregu, she tied her second-term bid to her first-term record. “I will not take the massive support I am enjoying from you for granted. Leadership comes with responsibility. We are campaigning on the strength of what we have achieved in the past and what I will do when given the opportunity again,” she said. At Ajaokuta Ward, she urged support for all PDP candidates and listened to Fulani communities asking for solar streetlights, boreholes and school blocks. She assured them their concerns would receive attention. “You must vote and defend your votes,” she said, urging constituents to watch the proper recording and uploading of results and the use of BVAS. Across the five local government areas, Adavi, Ajaokuta, Okehi, Okene and Ogori-Magongo, her campaign is built on work already done: water projects, solar streetlights, school devices, market infrastructure, digital connectivity and support for small businesses. In Ajaokuta Steel City, she donated learning iPads to Comprehensive Secondary School. In Adavi, on November 2, she took smart devices and laptops to OCSS Oboroke, Adavi Model Secondary School, Adavi Eba, and Community Secondary School, Obangede. item.title: FG eliminates 15,000 terrorists in 3yrs as 130,000 Boko Haram fighters surrender – APC-PCC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC on Sunday dusclosed that the military has eliminated more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits in the last three years, while more than 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and dependents have surrendered. Council Spokesperson, Dele Alake, said in a statement that the figures come from the scale of President Bola Tinubu’s ongoing military operations across the country. The President, he said, is determined to end the 17-year scourge of insecurity ravaging parts of Nigeria through a Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan. The fighters and dependents surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents. According to the statement, “the figures underscore the administration’s two-phase approach of sustained military operations and non-kinetic interventions to address insecurity.” The plan, it said, “provides a long-term framework for aligning defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development, and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges.” The statement described the initiative as a major component of the President’s determination to reposition the security architecture toward “a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled, and prevention-oriented system capable of addressing terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, and other forms of criminality.” On the military’s structure, the statement said President Tinubu has created four new Army divisions and restructured existing formations. The reforms, it said, “aim to expand operational coverage, decentralise military operations, and enable troops to respond more swiftly to security threats across the country.” The President has also approved two additional Army depots, in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State. Each can accommodate 6,000 recruits at a time, giving a combined training capacity of 12,000 soldiers. The Osogbo facility’s capacity is already being demonstrated, with 5,210 recruits currently undergoing training there. The expansion is expected “to reduce recruit turnaround time and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment.” President Tinubu has also approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers “to strengthen the military’s presence on the ground and enhance its operational effectiveness.” He approved the recruitment of 50,000 additional police officers as well, to reinforce internal security and improve policing capacity. item.title: Troops repel terrorists in Zamfara, kill suspect in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have repelled successive attacks by terrorists on communities in Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, with support from the Air Component, while recovering weapons and motorcycles in separate operations in Kaduna State. The operations, conducted on November 14, 2026, also resulted in the killing of one suspected terrorist in Kaduna and the recovery of two fabricated rifles, two motorcycles, a mobile phone and other items. The Joint Task Force, in a statement, said troops of Sector 2 responded swiftly to an attack by terrorists riding motorcycles on Wuya and Yarzabia communities in Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State. According to the statement, the troops engaged the attackers with superior firepower, forcing them to retreat. The terrorists, however, regrouped and launched a second wave of attacks but were again repelled by the troops, who maintained their defensive positions. Reinforcements subsequently arrived and extended operations to neighbouring communities, while troops sustained patrols to reassure residents and prevent further incursions. The task force said the Air Component of Operation Fansan Yamma also deployed a combat aircraft in a coordinated air-ground operation to support troops responding to the attacks. During the mission, the aircraft reportedly identified terrorists attempting to move a large herd of suspected rustled cattle away from the affected communities. The statement said the terrorists were engaged in multiple air strikes, resulting in the killing of scores of them. In a separate operation in Kaduna State, troops of Sector 1, acting on intelligence about suspected terrorist activities around farmlands in Aguba Village, Kajuru Local Government Area, conducted a fighting patrol to the area. The troops reportedly encountered the suspects and engaged them in a firefight, killing one, while others fled. A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two fabricated rifles, a mobile phone, substances suspected to be cannabis and other illicit drugs, as well as recharge cards. In another operation on the same day, troops acting on intelligence about the movement of terrorists along the Buruku-Kaduna Road encountered armed suspects and engaged them in a gun battle. The terrorists reportedly fled into a nearby forest, abandoning two motorcycles, which were recovered by the troops. The task force said troops had continued pursuit and exploitation operations to prevent the fleeing suspects from regrouping or carrying out further attacks. It described the operations as part of efforts to sustain pressure on terrorist groups, protect vulnerable communities and create a secure environment for farming and other socioeconomic activities across the North-West. The Theatre Command commended the troops for their resilience and fighting spirit, urging them to sustain the operational momentum. item.title: Sanusi, Ladoja seek national healing, warn against politicisation of traditional institutions
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful co-existence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning that the politicisation of traditional institutions poses a threat to their stability, historical relevance and role in fostering national unity. The two prominent traditional rulers made the call on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Oba Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, Ibadan, in an engagement that highlighted the need for traditional institutions to rise above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national cohesion. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic background, religious affiliation and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as part of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that the country could only achieve unity, progress and prosperity when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir explained that although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come.“ “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” Sanusi said. The Emir also apologised for the delay in visiting the Olubadan following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the revered throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. “It is only natural, coming to your kingdom, that I would pay this courtesy call. item.title: Customs to review Police Unit’s container escort mandate — Adeniyi
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) is considering a review of the mandate of its Customs Police Unit (CPU), particularly its responsibility for escorting containers in transit, following the adoption of advanced technology for cargo monitoring. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the Customs Police Unit Summit, which concluded in Abuja at the weekend. Adeniyi said the Service had acquired technology capable of monitoring containers from seaports to their destinations, including dry ports in the hinterland, making it necessary to reassess some of the unit’s traditional responsibilities. He recalled that the inauguration of the unit in 2019 generated agitation and resentment among some personnel, partly because of concerns about its assigned responsibilities. With technology providing more effective ways of monitoring cargo in transit, he said, the time had come to review the unit’s mandate and identify duties that could be performed more efficiently through modern systems. The Customs boss also stressed the need for collaboration with other security agencies and anti-corruption bodies, noting that effective Customs policing required expertise in intelligence gathering, surveillance, risk analysis and modern investigative techniques. He urged officers to respect human rights, observe due process and ensure the proper treatment of suspects. CPU must uphold integrity Addressing personnel of the unit, Adeniyi charged them to uphold discipline, restraint and integrity, describing these values as essential to protecting the reputation of the Service. “The red that you wear carries the trust of Nigerians and the reputation of the Service. Wear it with discipline, wear it with restraint, wear it with pride,” he said. He urged Customs officers to stay ahead of smugglers through intelligence-led operations, technology deployment and professionalism, warning that criminal networks were becoming increasingly sophisticated. According to him, the growing sophistication of criminal networks requires smarter enforcement strategies rather than continued reliance on conventional methods. “Criminal networks have grown more sophisticated. They use the same routes as legitimate traders to move firearm components, narcotics, fake medicines, protected wildlife and illicit funds, often through digital channels. Our answers must be smarter; they must not be harder,” he said. Adeniyi called for a more professional, accountable and technology-driven Customs Police Unit capable of addressing emerging security threats, combating illicit trade, strengthening institutional integrity and protecting the nation’s borders. item.title: Mammoth crowd welcomes Wali as Buni empowers over 500 youths, women in Yobe South
item.description: There was a mammoth crowd in Gadaka, Fika Local Government Area of Yobe State, on Thursday as the state government distributed empowerment items to over 500 youths and women across Yobe South Senatorial District (Zone B). The beneficiaries, drawn from the four local government areas in the zone, received motorcycles, tricycles (Jega) and sewing machines. The empowerment is aimed at promoting economic inclusion, supporting small businesses and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities. Beneficiaries and stakeholders at the event expressed appreciation for the intervention, saying it would boost economic activities at the grassroots. They also reaffirmed their support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Mai Mala Buni and the All Progressives Congress (APC), citing investments in road infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and peacebuilding across their communities. Speaking at the event, the APC governorship candidate in the state, Hon. Baba Mallam Wali, commended Governor Buni’s economic empowerment initiatives and pledged to sustain and consolidate them if elected in the 2027 general elections. Wali said the programme would be expanded to reach more youths and women across the state. Party leaders at the event also reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening party unity and working for the success of the APC at all levels, from the State House of Assembly to the Presidency.

item.title: Gunmen kidnap three travellers, shoot driver on Benue highway
item.description: By Peter Duru Armed men have reportedly kidnapped three travellers and shot a driver during an attack on a vehicle at Ijami village, Oglewu, Ohimini Local Government Area, LGA, of Benue State. The incident, which occurred at about 9:25pm on Saturday, involved seven persons travelling from Enugu to Abuja. The latest attack came barely days after a similar incident along the same axis, where a grieving man and his five friends were kidnapped while conveying the remains of his late wife from Kano for burial in neighbouring Okpokwu Local Government Area. In that incident, the kidnappers reportedly abandoned the corpse of the deceased on the highway before whisking her husband and his friends into the forest. They were subsequently released after a ransom was paid. Recounting the latest incident, an eyewitness, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the victims were attacked shortly after passing Otukpo on their way to Abuja. He said, “they were coming from Enugu and heading to Abuja on Saturday. At about 9:25pm, they got to a place called Ijami after Otukpo, under Oglewu. They were seven persons in the vehicle. The vehicle was attacked and the driver was shot. “He is in critical condition and currently receiving treatment in a hospital. Three of the passengers were taken into the forest by the armed men, while three of the passengers managed to escape. They have been seen and are in safe condition.” Expressing concern over the recurring attacks along the route, the eyewitness appealed to motorists to avoid travelling on the axis at night, blaming the deplorable condition of some roads for making it easier for criminals to operate. “We will continue to appeal to people to avoid these routes when night falls. Some of these roads are in deplorable condition, which makes it easy for the criminals to stop the vehicles and take away their victims. “We appeal that wherever you are coming from, pass the night in Otukpo and continue your trip the next day and be safe, rather than end up in the hands of armed men who will subject your family to unimaginable trauma to raise ransom money,” he said. Efforts to get the reaction of the Chairman of Ohimini Local Government Area, Gabriel Adole, were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to calls put across to his telephone. However, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, confirmed the incident. He said, “The victims were seven in number, three were rescued while three others are with the kidnappers. The driver was shot and he is receiving treatment at Teaching Hospital, Otukpo. “While efforts are on to secure the release of the other three, we urge the commuters to avoid night travels. Whenever it is night, look for somewhere and pass the night. The Commissioner had issued that advice and we expect that people, for their own safety, desist from night travels.” Vanguard News The post Gunmen kidnap three travellers, shoot driver on Benue highway appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu’s five-year defence plan ready to tackle insecurity – APC Campaign Council

The council said the plan would strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture, improve military effectiveness and provide a coordinated response to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other criminal activities. In a statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the initiative was designed to align defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges. It described the plan as part of Tinubu’s determination to reposition the country’s security system towards a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled and prevention-oriented framework. According to the statement, military operations conducted under the administration in the last three years have resulted in the elimination of more than 15,000 terrorists and bandits, while over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependants have surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents. The council said the figures reflected the administration’s two-pronged strategy of sustained military operations and non-kinetic interventions to address insecurity. On military expansion, the statement disclosed that Tinubu had approved the creation of four new Army divisions and the restructuring of existing formations to expand operational coverage and improve responses to security threats. It added that the President had also approved the establishment of two additional Army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to increase military training capacity and accelerate the recruitment of soldiers. According to the council, the two facilities can accommodate 6,000 recruits each, giving them a combined capacity of 12,000 soldiers at a time. The Osogbo facility, it said, currently has 5,210 recruits undergoing training. item.title: Nigeria’s unity must rise above ethnic, regional divisions – Sultan
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has challenged Nigerian Muslims to rise above ethnic, regional and social divisions and take greater responsibility for safeguarding national unity, promoting religious tolerance and confronting the security challenges threatening the country. The revered monarch warned that ethnicity, regional affiliations and differences in social backgrounds must never be allowed to undermine the unity of the Muslim Ummah or the collective responsibility of Nigerians to build a peaceful, stable and prosperous nation. He stressed that Muslims, irrespective of their ethnic origins or geographical locations, shared a common religious identity and must demonstrate, through their conduct and relationships, the unifying principles of Islam. The Sultan made the call on Sunday in Ibadan, Oyo State, while addressing participants at the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South-West Nigeria (MUSWEN), held at the M.O. Abdul Hall, University of Ibadan Central Mosque Auditorium. The assembly, which attracted Islamic leaders, traditional rulers, government representatives and other dignitaries, was held under the theme, “Insecurity in Nigeria: A Technology-Driven and Collective Approach for National Development.” Abubakar, who is also the President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), maintained that the survival and progress of the Muslim community depended largely on its ability to preserve its common identity and resist divisive tendencies capable of weakening its collective strength. According to him, the Almighty Allah created humanity as one family, making it imperative for Muslims to place their religious obligations and shared humanity above ethnic sentiments and other considerations. “We are one big family. Ethnicity should never be a determining factor in identifying who is a Muslim and who is not. Almighty Allah created us as one human family and commanded us to worship Him alone and glorify His name,” the Sultan said. He insisted that Islam must remain the guiding principle of Muslims’ lives, urging them not to allow political, ethnic or regional interests to displace the fundamental teachings of their faith. “It must be Islam first, Islam first, Islam first, and Islam last,” he declared. The Sultan further noted the equality of all human beings before Allah, explaining that neither ethnic background, social standing nor material possessions determined an individual’s worth in the sight of God. He said righteousness, piety and the fear of Allah remained the true standards by which human beings should be judged. “Before Allah, we are all equal. The best among us is the one who possesses the greatest degree of piety and righteousness,” he said. item.title: 2027 Grammys Nominations To Be Announced Monday
item.description: Nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, scheduled to hold in February 2027, will be announced on Monday, November 16, with Nigerian music fans able to follow the presentation from 1:45 p.m. West African Time (WAT). The Recording Academy will unveil nominees across all 100 categories during a special presentation led by its Chief Executive Officer, Harvey Mason Jr., and Chair of its Board of Trustees, Dr Chelsey Green. The announcement will begin at 7:45 a.m. Eastern Time (1:45 p.m. WAT), while the complete list of nominees is expected to be published around 9 a.m. Eastern Time (3 p.m. WAT). The presentation will be streamed live on Grammy.com and the official Grammys YouTube channel, with additional coverage on ABC’s Good Morning America. Several Grammy-winning and nominated artistes are expected to join Mason and Green in announcing the nominees. item.title: 2027: Atiku storms Bauchi communities, questions Tinubu’s grassroots outreach
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar weekend took his presidential campaign to communities across Bauchi State, drawing large crowds along his route from the airport to the Bauchi State Presidential Lodge and during a road trip to Azare. The tour, which featured a campaign rally, visits to four communities and courtesy calls on two traditional rulers, was part of his efforts to deepen grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections, while challenging President Bola Tinubu’s record of direct engagement with Nigerians. Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said Atiku began the day’s engagements at 8am with consultations with stakeholders before proceeding to an 11am rally in Bauchi. Atiku thanked residents for the reception, saying it had strengthened his resolve to take his message of affordable living and responsible leadership to communities across the country. After the rally, his campaign train travelled by road to Azare, stopping in Soro, Kari, Darazo and Misau, where residents turned out to welcome him and his entourage. In Misau, Atiku paid a courtesy visit to the Emir, Alhaji Ahmed Suleiman, thanking him and his council for their hospitality and words of encouragement. He also acknowledged residents who waited to receive his entourage despite its arrival at nightfall. He arrived in Azare at 10.30pm, where he paid a courtesy visit to the Emir of Katagum, extending his engagements with traditional rulers and community leaders. The campaign team is expected to proceed to Potiskum on Sunday for another rally. However, the ADC campaign used the reported scale of the reception to question Tinubu’s grassroots engagement, challenging the President to demonstrate a similar willingness to meet Nigerians directly. “The scale of yesterday’s welcome raises a simple question: can the sitting President volunteer to meet the people and make even half the effort Atiku has made to reach them?” Shaibu said. item.title: Bloody Spit: Ghana Waste Dump Poses Health, Environmental ‘Crisis’
item.description: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana’s capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water. At Agbogbloshie, a district on the Korle Lagoon delta, thousands of tonnes of refuse have accumulated over decades, overwhelming the fragile wetlands overlooking a slum of around 80,000 residents, many of them migrants and traders. For scrap dealer James Hassan, a 31-year-old Liberian immigrant, it is both his home and livelihood. Without gloves or a mask, he sifts daily through piles of unwanted electronics and metal for scraps to sell. The skin on his palms is thickened and scarred from cuts and rashes but he has become accustomed to the pain and discomfort. “I have headaches and coughs after long days under the sun, but I have never sought medical care. I feel they are normal,” he told AFP. Environmental health experts say that workers are exposed to toxic metals and chemicals through skin cuts, inhaling waste smoke and dust. Waste collectors dig through piles of waste at the Agbogbloshie dumpsite in Accra, on September 28, 2026. Photo by NIPAH DENNIS / AFP While no study as yet links specific diseases to Agbogbloshie’s pollution, “the cumulative contamination raises concern even if precise causal chains remain unquantified,” epidemiologist Reginald Quansah, of the University of Ghana, said. Global Pipeline Of Waste Waste management is a prominent theme at the COP31 climate talks, which began in Turkey on Monday. Agbogbloshie’s refuse comes largely from beyond Ghana’s borders. Accra’s huge second-hand clothing market has imports from Europe, North America and Asia — but often with a troubling byproduct. “A lot of clothes that are shipped into Ghana come as waste,” Greenpeace Africa’s head of investigations Samuel Quashie-Idun told AFP. Greenpeace estimates that 15 million used garments arrive in Ghana each week. Even after traders extract what they can sell, roughly half ends up as “dead waste” dumped on beaches and fields or burned, it said. One study Greenpeace cited put Ghana’s used clothing imports at over 110,000 tonnes in 2022. For the country’s 35 million people, “these volumes far exceed local demand and… burdens waste systems,” Quashie-Idun said. Greenpeace found that 89 percent of sampled “dead” garments contained petrochemical fibres such as polyester, which shed microplastics as they decay, and release carcinogens hundreds of times above safe levels in smoke when the textiles are burned. “This is not just an environmental crisis… it’s also a human health crisis,” said Hellen Kahaso Dena, Greenpeace’s plastics project expert. ‘Fashion Waste Dumping Ground’ “The global north is effectively using Ghana as a dumping ground for fashion waste,” she told AFP. item.title: Cabo Verde Votes In Presidential Election As Incumbent Seeks Second Term
item.description: Cabo Verde voted for a new president on Sunday, with incumbent Jose Maria Neves favoured to win a second term as head of state of the West African archipelago renowned for its democratic stability. He is facing the country’s first woman candidate, Joana Rosa Amado, among other contenders. Voting started at 0900 GMT and ends at 1900 GMT. Provisional results are expected overnight. “I’ve voted. Now I’m going to mass, and I believe everything will go well — normally and with civic-mindedness,” Adilia Gomes, 55, told AFP after casting her ballot in the capital, Praia. “Everything went normally despite a few minutes’ delay in the opening of my polling station,” added another voter, Claudino Semedo. Nearly 420,000 people are eligible to vote. The election is being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union. A supporter of Cape Verde’s President and presidential candidate Jose Maria Neves waves a flag bearing his image during a campaign rally in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on October 30, 2026.(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) Cabo Verde, located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometres (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal, comprises 10 volcanic islands and is an increasingly popular tourist destination. It made world headlines this year when its national football team reached the knockout stages in its first World Cup, and when a cruise ship containing people with hantavirus docked off its shores. Stability, Hospitality Unlike several of its West African neighbours where presidential elections have been tense in recent years, Cabo Verde is known for its political stability and good governance. It is considered a model of democracy in Africa, with strong economic growth. A voter queues at a polling station during Cape Verde’s presidential election in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on November 15, 2026(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) The country is known for its “morabeza” (“hospitality”, in local creole), openness, and carnivals. It also has its own style of music. According to the Mo Ibrahim Foundation 2026 index on global governance, Cabo Verde ranks third out of 54 countries on the continent. Politically, it has a semi-presidential system in which the executive is dominated by the prime minister. The president does not govern but acts more as an arbiter, working to guarantee unity and uphold the constitution. The head of state appoints the prime minister based on the results of legislative elections and represents the country abroad. item.title: Fela, Queen Latifah, Phil Collins Join Rock Hall Of Fame
item.description: Afrobeat pioneer Fela Kuti, rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan and punk rocker Billy Idol were among the music luminaries inducted Saturday into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame at a star-studded concert gala. The versatile Phil Collins, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order, and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross also joined the rock pantheon at the ceremony held in Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater. But several of the 2026 class of artists — Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden — skipped the night celebrating their honor, one of the music industry’s most prestigious. But the show went on. Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan — the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences — brought the ruckus, performing their own hits including “C.R.E.A.M” and “Wu‐Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” said member Method Man onstage to resounding cheers. To the haters, he said, “you can kiss my inducted ass.” It proved a banner night for women in hip-hop, with honorees including Queen Latifah as well as MC Lyte, who is widely recognized as the “First Lady of Hip Hop.” The storied performers tore up the stage with a medley of their hits, before Megan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma joined them to underscore the legacy of women in rap. Travis Barker, the drummer from Blink-182, inducted Collins, drawing tears from the British artist who attended the ceremony alongside his children, including Lily of “Emily in Paris” fame. US rapper/actress Queen Latifah attends the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on November 14, 2026. (Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) Collins — whose entry into the hall is his second, the first was as part of the band Genesis — walked to the stage with two canes, taking the mic and saying, “I’m really not as bad as it looks.” “You haven’t heard the last of me, I can promise you that.” Cynthia Erivo belted out Collins’s smash “In The Air Tonight,” with Barker playing the instantly recognizable drum fill. “My life has just been one thing after the other, one dream after the other,” Collins said to journalists backstage. item.title: 2027: SERAP Gives INEC Seven Days To Prosecute Electoral Violence Suspects
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has given the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) seven days to prosecute persons arrested over reported incidents of electoral and political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections or face legal action. SERAP made the demand in a letter dated November 14, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, urging the commission to obtain relevant case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and prosecute suspects where sufficient evidence exists. The organisation also asked INEC to direct its legal officers or appointed legal practitioners to review the files and promptly initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows several reported incidents of political violence across the country since campaigns for the 2027 elections began on 19 August, including the latest attack on members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November. In the letter signed by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP urged Amupitan to press the police to conclude investigations into other reported attacks, arrest suspected perpetrators and their sponsors, and forward relevant evidence to INEC. It also called on the commission to exercise its powers under Section 83 of the Electoral Act 2026 to demand explanations from political parties suspected of involvement in or encouraging prohibited conduct and impose prescribed fines on those that fail to comply with lawful directives. SERAP expressed concern over reports of attacks on political convoys, party secretariats, rallies and meetings, as well as intimidation of candidates and supporters. Cited incidents included the reported obstruction of the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Benue State on 8 September; attacks on political meetings in Enugu State on 12 September; and the attack on the convoy of ADC senatorial candidate Herberta Okonofua in Edo State on 6 October. Others included attacks on supporters of Accord governorship candidate Oriyomi Hamzat in Ibadan on 14 October, which reportedly resulted in one death, and the attack on the convoy of NDC candidate Rollins Offia-Nwali in Ebonyi State on 22 October, which allegedly left one person dead and three injured. The organisation also cited the reported attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and his team in Ado-Ekiti on 30 October, the attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar on 4 November, and an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November, which reportedly left one person dead and five injured. It added that journalist Samuel Adebanjo was assaulted and his equipment seized while covering the November 12 incident in Lagos.
